subject: HealTech hosting pathing and HIPAA evidence — next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@healtech.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:10:00Z
Subject: HealTech hosting pathing and HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Maria — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

- Primary constraint: you confirmed HealTech will process PHI and needs a HIPAA-compliant deployment and a signed BAA.
- Hosting options under consideration: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity (isolation + SLA), Private VPC/on-prem (full network isolation).
- Risk posture: your security team prefers customer-managed network controls and key management for production PHI; they flagged SOC 2 Type II evidence and a vendor penetration test report as gating items.

What Redwood can provide today (short version): 
- SOC 2 Type II summary + auditor contact (attached summary). Full report available under NDA.
- Draft BAA for review (attached). We typically sign when a Dedicated or Private deployment is chosen; hosted API customers can also execute a BAA in some accounts with specific DLP controls.
- Private VPC option supports customer VPC peering and BYOK via KMS; on-prem is available but will add ~8–12 weeks for packaging and validation.

Proposed next steps (we recommend a 2-track approach so security gets what they need while we keep momentum):
1) Security intake pack: I will share the SOC2 summary, BAA draft, and a short technical runbook for our Private VPC configuration. (Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, BAA-draft-HealTech-v1.docx)
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 45-minute session next week with your security and infra (we suggested Wed 4/21 or Thu 4/22). Goal: confirm KMS options and network topology requirements.
3) Mutual action plan: we'll draft a short MAP with milestones (security review, BAA, pilot, SLA onboarding). I attached an initial MAP spreadsheet — please tell us if the dates look realistic.

Open questions from our side that will help narrow to Dedicated vs Private: 
- Will HealTech require customer-managed KMS/HSM (BYOK) for all PHI models or only for production keys?
- Do you need on-prem hosting for regulatory reasons, or is VPC with strict egress controls acceptable?

I copied Markus (security lead) and Laura (solutions engineering) to help with the technical Q&A. If you want, we can start the NDA flow so we can share the full SOC2 bundle.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options after I hear back on preferred days.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments (stubs): redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); BAA-draft-HealTech-v1.docx (DOCX)
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@healtech.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: HealTech Security <security@healtech.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T20:37:00Z
Subject: Re: HealTech hosting pathing and HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Thanks, Avery — appreciate the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our security team (copied):

- Primary must-haves: signed BAA, SOC 2 Type II full report (not just summary), evidence of data residency controls, and network isolation (VPC peering is preferred).
- KMS: production keys must be customer-managed (BYOK) or HSM-backed; development keys can be Redwood-managed with appropriate labeling.
- Pen testing: we need confirmation of recent vendor pentest (last 12 months) and remediation notes.

On hosting: our default is Private VPC peering with strict egress ACLs. On-prem would be considered if VPC peering cannot satisfy our controls.

We are available for the technical deep-dive on Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 PT. Please send an invite and any pre-read. Also — can you confirm if Redwood supports DocuSign-based BAAs or do we need a wet-sign workflow?

Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Product & Ops | HealTech Solutions
maria.gomez@healtech.com | +1 (718) 555-0199

--
On Apr 18, 2027, at 15:10, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T02:15:00Z
Subject: Re: HealTech hosting pathing and HIPAA evidence — internal notes

Avery — quick internal note before the call on Thu:

- I reviewed HealTech's requirements. We can meet BYOK via a KMS integration for Private VPC and Dedicated Reserved options. BYOK for Hosted API is limited and typically requires an enterprise contract plus network isolation add-ons.
- SOC2: the full report is NDA-gated. We should request a short MSA/NDA before sending the full Type II. I will prepare the pentest summary and remediation timeline.
- Timeline: if HealTech chooses Private VPC, expect ~6–9 weeks for VPC peering and key validation (less if they accept a Dedicated pool with strict tenancy). On-prem has more variable lead time (8–12 weeks for packaging and validation).

I'll join the Thu deep-dive and bring the KMS integration sheet. Laura — can you prep the MAP with realistic sprint dates (we can iterate in the call)?

-Markus

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@healtech.com>, HealTech Security <security@healtech.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T18:02:00Z
Subject: HealTech — maps, pre-read and calendar invite for Thu 4/22 10:00 PT

Maria / team — thanks, confirmed for Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 PT. Calendar invite sent separately. Quick pre-read and action items attached: 

1) Attached: mutual-action-plan-HT-v1.xlsx — I populated an initial 6-week timeline that assumes Private VPC peering as the target. Review the milestone "BAA signed" and "KMS BYOK validation" dates and tell me if your legal/security timelines differ.
2) Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and BAA-draft-HealTech-v1.docx. Per Markus, the full SOC2 report is NDA-gated — if you confirm NDA/MSA intake we can start the secure artifact transfer during the call.
3) Pentest: I pulled the pentest executive summary; I'll share it in the secure folder right after the call.

DocuSign: yes, we support DocuSign for BAAs. We also accept signed PDFs if your legal prefers that route.

Proposed agenda for Thu 4/22 (45 min):
- 5 min: introductions and goals
- 10 min: Redwood KMS options + network topologies (Markus)
- 15 min: HealTech security Q&A on evidence and controls (Maria + security)
- 10 min: MAP review and next milestones (Laura)
- 5 min: actions and owners

Please reply if you want additional items added to the agenda. After the meeting, we'll upload the full SOC2 under NDA and update the MAP.

Best,
Avery

Attachments (stubs): mutual-action-plan-HT-v1.xlsx (XLSX); redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); BAA-draft-HealTech-v1.docx (DOCX)
